title: Normalize prefetch and batch metering for correct quota and billing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Observed discrepancies between billed token counts and actual upstream compute when prefix/kv cache hits and aggressive batching/prefetching are enabled. Some customers are underbilled (shared cached responses attributed to wrong tenant) while others are overbilled due to double-counting in batch aggregation windows. This ticket establishes a deterministic attribution and aggregation model to correct metering for: prefix caches (prefix match hits), KV cache single-key hits across multi-tenant batches, and prefetching/pipelined requests that consume capacity but should not be charged to end-customer quotas in the same way as generated tokens.
background: Recent postmortem from a large customer flagged two issues: 1) Prefix cache hit responses were not consistently attributed to the original requester when responses were served from a shared cache node, and 2) the batch aggregator sometimes counted the same KV-cache-resolved tokens multiple times across sub-requests when a batch contained duplicated keys. Runtime change in 1.20 made prefetching more aggressive which exposed the attribution gap. Lines of evidence: billing mismatch dashboard (billing.team/dashboards/billing-integrity-2026-03), customer report #CUST-982, and sampling traces (trace ids in links).
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce per-entry attribution metadata in cache entries: origin_customer, origin_request_id, and last_used_window. 2) When serving from prefix or KV cache, charge the token/embedding unit to the origin_customer if present. 3) If cache entry is marked as "shared-prefetch" (pre-warmed without direct request) then charge to 'system-prefetch' bucket and surface a separate cost line item (not charged against customer quotas) for internal prefetch budget. 4) Update batch aggregation: deduplicate KV keys within a batch and attribute the resolved token cost only once to the requesting customer(s) according to a deterministic split rule when multiple customers share a single resolution (prefer origin_customer, else split by tokens_requested). 5) Ensure rate limiter consumes from per-tenant quota only for tokens actually attributable to that tenant. 6) Add migration script to reprocess last 30 days of ingested metering events to backfill corrected charges for impacted invoices.
tradeoffs: Accuracy vs overhead: adding attribution headers to cache entries increases memory and metadata size; we must cap the size and evict attribution metadata for low-value entries.

Performance impact: deduplication and attribution logic adds CPU in the hot path; we'll implement a fast-path for single-tenant batches and an async reconciliation worker for cross-tenant complex cases.
Billing complexity: introducing 'system-prefetch' bucket may confuse customers initially; docs and console UI updates required to explain internal prefetch budgeting.
Backward compatibility: older cache entries lack attribution; fallback heuristics will be used until migration completes which may cause small transient billing variance.
Data retention: storing origin_request_id has privacy implications; will not persist PII and will rotate attribution metadata per retention policy.
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests that cover prefix cache hit attribution for single-tenant and multi-tenant scenarios
E2E test simulating duplicated KV keys in a batch results in a single metering event with correct attribution
Billing dashboard (billing.team/dashboards/billing-integrity-2026-03) shows <0.1% variance vs ground-truth synthetic traffic after rollout
Rate limiter only deducts quota for tokens attributed to tenant; verified with synthetic traffic harness
Migration job runs and backfills sample dataset with expected corrected charges; migration plan approved by finance
Documentation and Console UI feature flag added: 'Show prefetch/system cost' and 'Show cache attribution'

progress_updates: 2026-03-11: Design review - agreed on per-entry attribution fields but capped size to 128 bytes metadata to limit RAM impact. Action: add eviction policy by entry-score.
2026-03-12: Marcus opened PR 4521 with runtime changes; includes fast-path where single-tenant entries are charged inline without extra dedupe.

2026-03-13: Batcher prototype merged to feature branch; found a race where two concurrent batches could both claim credit for same KV resolution when origin_customer is absent. Decided to add lightweight lease token to KV cache resolution step.
2026-03-14: Billing pipeline team validated new metering event schema; finance requested a conservative rollback window option for first invoice cycle after rollout.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased memory pressure on cache nodes. Mitigation: metadata size cap + LRU eviction and 'metadata-lite' mode for low-value keys.

Risk: Rollout causes unexpected invoice diffs. Mitigation: opt-in rollout via feature flag and dry-run mode that emits debugging events but does not change invoices; reconciliation job to generate patch invoices if needed.
Risk: Performance regression in 99th percentile latency. Mitigation: benchmark fast-path vs full attribution path and gate full attribution behind sampling initially.
Risk: Customer confusion about 'system-prefetch' costs. Mitigation: product will add console messaging, changelog, and optional migration credits for early impacted customers.
